recommendation: Keep this no-change audit as-is. Future work on process-priority code-system ownership, experimental status, or binding strength should proceed under the later FM tickets rather than reopening the already-applied Claim.priority definition correction.
issue_request: FHIR-20172 was a Published/Persuasive Financial Management change request asking that Claim.priority match the process-priority value set, with the definition "The provider-required urgency of processing the request. Typical values include: stat, normal, deferred."
initial_application: No Jira-keyed source commit was found for FHIR-20172. Git pickaxe history shows the requested Claim.priority wording was introduced in source/claim/structuredefinition-Claim.xml by f952b5321de9cdbcb7b2521862890c757e21d530, a broad 2022 FHIR core update that also corrected nearby priority/comment typos before R5 publication.
additional_context: Claim is an active resource in source/fhir.ini, and the current Claim.priority element binds to ValueSet/process-priority with the requested definition. FHIR-37907, the parallel ExplanationOfBenefit.priority wording issue, is already represented on the combined branch. Later process-priority tickets FHIR-50906 and FHIR-49887 remain Resolved - change required/ToBeApplied context and do not change this Published R5 definition audit.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current build-scope Claim source already satisfies the issue and no source edit is necessary.

related_jiras.note: A separate combined-branch commit already audits/fixes the parallel ExplanationOfBenefit.priority wording for the same process-priority examples.

Later FM R6 ticket proposes changing process-priority to a standard CodeSystem and binding to extensible, but it is Resolved - change required/ToBeApplied and does not alter this Published R5 Claim definition audit.
Later FM R6 ticket concerns removing the experimental flag for process-priority, but it is Resolved - change required/ToBeApplied and is outside the seed request.
Earlier Published DSTU1 tracker identified lower-case/deferred wording errors in Claim.priority, showing the same historical problem family but not requiring a separate current reconciliation here.
